newQuestions.sourceExcerpt: May be SC or IV depending on the order
newQuestions.point: Identify IV and SC as UFH administration routes; do not infer regimen interchangeability.

newQuestions.sourceExcerpt: Therapeutic IV infusion requires a controlled pump
newQuestions.point: Recall the device required to control a continuous therapeutic UFH infusion.
Recognize the need for platelet surveillance during UFH even when coagulation response is therapeutic.
Identify prior severe reaction to another 5-HT3 antagonist as a specific hypersensitivity review concern.
Recognize tramadol as a serotonergic co-medication requiring serotonin-syndrome vigilance with ondansetron.
Identify bradyarrhythmia as an ondansetron ECG-monitoring risk independent of other stated factors.
Recall the required monitoring during IV verapamil rather than receiving it as a stem hint.
Recognize sodium/water depletion and hypotension as risks of excessive furosemide diuresis.

newQuestions.sourceExcerpt: Do not give IV verapamil close to an IV beta-blocker dose
newQuestions.point: Recognize the contraindicated close administration of IV verapamil and an IV beta blocker.
Recognize a QT-prolonging co-medication as an independent ondansetron monitoring concern.
Recognize the antianginal role independently from rate control.

revisedQuestions.point: Respond promptly to major bleeding during UFH infusion.
Recognize bradycardia, AV block and significant hypotension as verapamil adverse effects.
Identify L-type calcium-channel blockade in the AV node and myocardium.
Locate furosemide action at the Na-K-2Cl transporter in the thick ascending loop of Henle.
Test heart failure independently rather than crediting a combined HF-plus-amiodarone scenario for both facts.
Remove the ECG/BP answer from the time-question stem so it does not disclose the separate monitoring answer.
Correct enalapril name in captopril question; no new clinical conclusion or complete captopril audit is claimed.
Require both coagulation-test selection and understanding of variable response in a paired question.
